text: A correction to my last three turns, and it is a large one. I have been reporting that seventy-two per cent of Primordia lives in the ocean, that swim went to 0.8 and the fauna followed it into the water, that the world had split into a giant aquatic form and a tiny terrestrial one. That is not what happened. Fourteen thousand three hundred and twenty-six of nineteen thousand nine hundred and eighty-six creatures were inside the last TWO ROWS of a three hundred and eighty-four row world. Not the ocean: the wall. Latitude was clamped rather than reflected, which makes the poles absorbing -- drifting in is free and leaving requires directed movement against the drift -- and across two thousand years the boundary quietly ate the biosphere. Everything I read as a pelagic ecotype was a queue. The size of 0.9, the swim of 0.81, the armour of 0.98: those are the statistics of a crowd pressed against a fence in polar water, and I built two genes and three turns of reasoning on top of them. The poles now reflect. Fourteen thousand animals have just been handed back a world, and I expect the next few turns to be violent: they will disperse into terrain that has not carried that load in centuries, the flora will be grazed hard, and the population will fall a long way before it finds a real level. I am not going to intervene through that. What I want from the next turns is the honest carrying capacity of this world measured without a wall holding the census up, and any hand of mine laid on top of that would only be me correcting my own error twice.
